summary: Elk County, PA lookout on State Game Lands 44: a 2018 100-ft steel tower beside a stone cabin; the original was a 1939 Aermotor, and 1921 papers describe earlier steel.

facts.design: 100-foot steel structure (2018 replacement); the original tower was a 100-foot Aermotor

events.note: Newspaper items describe a steel lookout tower being built on Boot Jack by the state forestry department
October 1921 item says a man would be stationed on the tower in fall and spring dry seasons (a planned seasonal lookout post)
Watchman said dense smoke made any view of the landscape beyond a mile impossible
Register gives the original tower as a 100-foot Aermotor built in 1939
June 1939 item reports the tower was raised from sixty feet to a height printed as 'eight-six feet' (not checked against a second source)
Original tower removed; replaced by a new 100-foot steel structure; stone observer's cabin remains on site
Register's Built field for the current steel structure
Registered March 24, 2020; nominated by Robert McKay

corrections.proposed: 100-foot steel structure (2018 replacement); original tower was an Aermotor
corrections.why: The register describes the 2018 structure as a new 100-foot steel structure and the Aermotor as the original tower that was removed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 2018 date is the current steel structure. The register dates the original Aermotor to 1939, and 1921 newspaper items describe an earlier steel tower on the site. Whether the 1939 raising in the Forest Lookouts item is the same structure as the register's Aermotor is not settled by these sources.

sources.title: DCNR Initiative To Replace, Renovate Fire Towers Across The State

notes_for_editor: The record's design 'Aermotor' describes the original tower; the register gives the current structure as steel (proposed correction, for human review). Unreconciled: the register's 1939 Aermotor date versus the Forest Lookouts' 1939 raising to a height printed as 'eight-six feet' (OCR or typo, unchecked), and whether 1921 steel is the same site. The PA Fire Towers StoryMap and MapSeries pages returned no text (JavaScript only), so the record's pa_storymap 1939 claim is unchecked. The DCNR 16-tower program is given as context; the blog's text we read does not name Boot Jack, and it covers state forestland while Boot Jack is on State Game Lands. No public access or current condition source found, so access is omitted. Used 2 WebSearch calls and about 7 fetches (6 distinct pages plus a repeat grep), one over the per-tower budget.
